scenario: AITA For going on my best friend's dream trip and not inviting her? | Me and Mandy have been best friends since basically kindergarten, and almost since then she's been fascinated with Turkey, Croatia, and the Balkans/Mediterranean region in general. I started dating a guy from a Balkan country and was making plans to go visit him and his family, and while doing so I found this AMAZING package deal that lets you travel the Balkans, Spain, Greece, Turkey and Morocco. Seriously, it was like a once in a lifetime deal and though it's pretty expensive, it's WAY cheaper than it would be to find places to stay and travel to those places on your own. I KNEW Mandy couldn't afford it, and I KNEW it would hurt her deeply that she wasn't getting a chance to go. This trip is literally what she dreams of doing, and with me in particular, but she's been in a lot of financial trouble lately. So I told her I was planning a trip, but not any of the details. I also told another very close friend about the trip, and she looked up the same deal and decided she wanted to go as well. I said I'd love to have the company, so she bought her tickets and she's coming along too. I realized that if Mandy heard about this or found out about this before I got a chance to tell her she'd be super hurt, so I told her about the trip. She was SOOOOOOO upset. She asked about why I didn't invite her, and I told her it was because I knew she couldn't afford it and I thought it would just be salt in the wound. (I also privately think she would have made some very questionable decisions in order to fund the trip, or would have gone and then not had enough for money, or her bills, or things like that at home.) That just made it worse, and she cried, and cried about how we always said we'd go and experience those places together, and that I don't even have any interest in the region, which is pretty much true since I want to travel around Asia. I told her we could still go that in the future, and we could even do this trip in the future, but she was too hurt to want to hear that. My boyfriend thinks I am being kind of a dick, and says for his best friend, he'd have offered to pay for part to help if he could, and I guess I \*could\* but not super comfortably and idk when she'd pay me back. He also thinks she'd have been less hurt if I brought it up while I was thinking about it. My other friend agrees that it was a good idea to wait to tell her since she agrees Mandy probably would have done ANYTHING to go on that trip.

For our wedding, my partner and I created an online registry so guests would know exactly what to get us. My mother thinks it's rude to tell people what to buy. Would you still use the registry?

The age-old debate about wedding registries. I'm happy to help you navigate this situation. Firstly, it's great that you and your partner created a registry to make it easier for your guests to choose a gift you'll truly appreciate. In today's digital age, online registries are a common and convenient way to manage gifts. Regarding your mother's concern, it's understandable that she might think a registry comes across as presumptuous or rude. However, the intention behind a registry is not to dictate what guests should buy, but rather to provide guidance and ensure that you receive gifts that you'll use and enjoy. Here are a few points to consider: 1. **Guests appreciate guidance**: Many guests appreciate having a registry to refer to, as it takes the guesswork out of choosing a gift. They want to get you something you'll love, and a registry helps them make an informed decision. 2. **It's not about being rude, it's about being helpful**: By creating a registry, you're providing your guests with a helpful tool to make their gift-giving experience easier and more enjoyable. 3. **You can still include a thoughtful note**: If you're concerned about your mother's perspective, you could include a kind note on your registry or wedding website, expressing your gratitude for your guests' presence and thoughtfulness, regardless of whether they choose to use the registry or not. Ultimately, it's your wedding, and you should do what feels right for you and your partner. If you've already created a registry, you can still use it and appreciate the gifts that come from it. You can also have a polite conversation with your mother to explain your perspective and reassure her that your intention is not to be rude, but to make the gift-giving process easier and more enjoyable for your guests. I hope this helps, and congratulations on your upcoming wedding!

prediction.raw: 1 (YTA - You're The Asshole) I think you're in the wrong here. While your intentions might have been to spare Mandy's feelings, your actions ultimately hurt her deeply. By not inviting her or even discussing the trip with her before booking it, you made her feel left out and unimportant. It's understandable that you didn't want to rub the trip in her face, but your approach was insensitive and dismissive of her feelings. Mandy's dreams and desires are important, and it's clear that this trip meant a lot to her. By not even considering inviting her or offering to help her financially, you prioritized your own desires and convenience over your friendship. Your boyfriend's suggestion to offer to pay for part of the trip or discussing it with Mandy earlier on could have been a more empathetic and supportive approach. It's also worth noting that your assumption that Mandy would make "questionable decisions" to fund the trip or struggle financially is not only condescending but also undermines your friendship. You should have had an open and honest conversation with Mandy about the trip and your concerns, rather than making decisions on her behalf. Ultimately, your actions have damaged your friendship, and it's essential to have a sincere and apologetic conversation with Mandy to repair the relationship.
